title: Apache, Mod_Proxy, & 4D
author: Timothy Penner, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note explains how to reverse-proxy Apache to 4D's built-in web server using mod_proxy, a well-established and still widely used Apache module; the general reverse-proxy technique (ProxyPass/ProxyPassReverse) remains valid and is still a common deployment pattern for fronting an application server with Apache or nginx today. The SOAP-specific example (proxying /4DSOAP requests and manually patching the WSDL's soap:address) is dated, however, since 4D's web services story has since shifted heavily toward REST and ORDA-based data access, making raw SOAP/WSDL considerations far less central. The core Apache configuration knowledge is still directly applicable, but the SOAP use case has faded in relevance.
related_updates: REST + ORDA (4D v16 R5+, 2017) largely superseded SOAP as 4D's primary web-service integration approach
4D's web server has since gained more built-in HTTPS/reverse-proxy-friendly options, reducing some (not all) of the need for a separate Apache front end
